items.title: Introducing GPT-6.1 Sol
items.summary_1line: Meet GPT-6.1 Sol: near-Astra intelligence for coding, computer use, and professional work at one-fifth of Astra’s standard API input and output token prices.
items.editor_note: OpenAI's launch post: near-Astra intelligence at one-fifth of Astra's API prices.

items.title: Asana cuts model costs 76x in browser tests with GPT-6.1 Sol
items.summary_1line: Using GPT-6 Astra in Codex, Asana made its browser agent 76x cheaper and 5x faster in tests to offer customers more capable models.
items.editor_note: First customer numbers: Asana's browser agent 76x cheaper and 5x faster in tests.

items.summary_1line: Codex CLI Defaults to GPT-6.1 Sol, Cuts Price 80% [2026] tech-insider.org
items.editor_note: Secondary report that Codex CLI now defaults to GPT-6.1 Sol with an 80% price cut.

items.title: Codex CLI Defaults to GPT-6.1 Sol, 77% Cheaper [2026]
items.summary_1line: Codex CLI Defaults to GPT-6.1 Sol, 77% Cheaper [2026] tech-insider.org
items.editor_note: Same outlet's follow-up restating the Codex CLI default with a 77% price cut instead of 80%.

editorial.tldr: OpenAI introduced GPT-6.1 Sol on Sep 29, pitching near-Astra intelligence for coding and computer use at one-fifth of Astra's API token prices. On Oct 9 Asana reported its browser agent 76x cheaper and 5x faster in tests.
editorial.whats_new: A second tech-insider.org post now puts the reported Codex CLI default switch to GPT-6.1 Sol at 77% cheaper, down from 80% two days earlier; OpenAI has not confirmed either figure.
editorial.why_it_matters: GPT-6.1 Sol lowers the price of Astra-class coding and computer-use work, so routing and cost-per-task assumptions built on Astra pricing are out of date.
editorial.take_for_builders: Treat the Codex CLI price cut as unconfirmed: rerun your coding and computer-use evals on GPT-6.1 Sol against your Astra baseline on cost per completed task, and check OpenAI's pricing page before changing any default model.

status.detail: GPT-6.1 Sol has moved from launch to a customer cost claim and a reported Codex CLI default whose price cut is still unconfirmed (80%, then 77%).
